facts.name: Program description
facts.detail: Official M.S. degree page: graduate programs let students study computing areas, conduct specialized research, and make original contributions.
facts.quote: Graduate degree programs in the Department of Computer Science provide students the opportunity to study different subject areas of computing science, conduct research in specialized areas, and make original contributions to the field.

facts.name: Available tracks
facts.detail: The degree page lists thesis, project, integrated BS-MS, and several exam tracks.
facts.quote: Available Options Thesis Track Project Track Integrated BS-MS Track

facts.name: Exam-track options
facts.detail: Exam tracks named on the degree page include Foundations and Theory, Cyber Security, AI and Machine Learning, Software Engineering, Data Science and Big Data, Database and Information Retrieval, Graphics and Augmented Reality, and Programming Language and Systems.
facts.quote: Exam Track - Foundations and Theory Exam Track - Cyber Security Exam Track - AI and Machine Learning

facts.name: Study areas
facts.detail: The degree page lists study areas including algorithms, operating and distributed systems, architecture and networking, computational geometry and robotics, graphics and image processing, programming languages, AI, databases, and software engineering.
facts.quote: Our master's program gives you the opportunity to study different areas, including: Design and analysis of algorithms.

facts.name: 30-credit minimum and grade floor
facts.detail: Department master's-requirements page: students must pass at least 30 credits of 600- and 700-level courses with a grade of C or better.
facts.quote: you must pass at least 30 credits of 600- and 700-level courses with a grade of C or better

facts.name: At least 24 credits in computer science
facts.detail: Department requirements: at least 24 credits must be in computer science.
facts.quote: At least 24 credits must be in computer science.

facts.name: 700-level computer science minimum (department page)
facts.detail: Department requirements: at least 18 credits of computer science courses must be at the 700 level. The 2026–27 plans of study also quote a Graduate College 50-percent 700-level rule; both are reported.
facts.quote: At least 18 credits of computer science courses must be at the 700 level.

facts.name: Required CS 656, 660, and 677 if not already taken
facts.detail: If equivalent courses have not been taken previously, CS 656, 660, and 677 must be included.
facts.quote: If equivalent courses have not been taken previously, CS 656, 660, and 677 must be included.

facts.name: Thesis or project credit cap
facts.detail: At most six credits of CS 791 (thesis) or three credits of CS 790 (project) can be included.
facts.quote: At most, six credits of CS 791 (Thesis Option) or three credits of CS 790 (Project Option) can be included.

facts.name: 3.0 GPA while in the program
facts.detail: A GPA of 3.0 or higher must be maintained; below that, probation, then possible drop if it stays below 3.0 the next regular semester.
facts.quote: A GPA of 3.0 or higher must be maintained at all times while in the program.

facts.name: 2026-27 thesis subplan units
facts.detail: 2026-27 thesis plan of study (header: UNLV Graduate College 2026-2027 Catalog): 24 credits of 600- or 700-level CS courses (up to 3 credits outside CS) plus 6 credits of CS 791; minimum 30 credits.
facts.quote: Complete 24 credits of 600- or 700- level Computer Science (CS) courses. Students may complete up to 3 credits outside of CS.

facts.name: CS 791 thesis
facts.detail: 2026-27 thesis plan lists CS 791 for the 6-credit thesis requirement.

facts.name: Thesis plan graduation minimum
facts.detail: Thesis plan: minimum credits required for graduation = 30.

facts.name: 2026-27 project subplan units
facts.detail: 2026-27 project plan: 27 credits of 600- or 700-level CS courses (up to 3 outside CS) plus 3 credits of CS 790; minimum 30 credits.
facts.quote: Complete 27 credits of 600- or 700- level Computer Science (CS) courses. Students may complete up to 3 credits outside of CS.

facts.name: CS 790 project
facts.detail: 2026-27 project plan lists CS 790 for the 3-credit project requirement.

facts.name: Graduate College 700-level share (plans of study)
facts.detail: The 2026-27 plans of study state that a minimum of 50 percent of the degree program must be 700-level courses, excluding thesis, dissertation, or professional/scholarly paper. This sits beside the department page's 'at least 18 credits of computer science courses must be at the 700 level.'
facts.quote: A minimum of 50 percent of the degree program must be 700-level courses excluding thesis, dissertation, or professional/scholarly paper.
facts.rejectedReason: Rejected by the user 2026-11-13: keep department rule (at least 18 CS credits at 700-level). Graduate College 50% 700-level plan-of-study fact was not kept.

facts.name: Exam track Foundations and Theory required list
facts.detail: 2026-27 Foundations and Theory exam plan: complete 9 credits from CS 656, CS 677, CS 715, CS 758, and CS 789, plus 21 credits of other 600- or 700-level CS courses.

facts.name: CS 656 on the Foundations exam list
facts.detail: The Foundations and Theory plan lists CS 656 among the required-course options.

facts.name: CS 677 on the Foundations exam list
facts.detail: The Foundations and Theory plan lists CS 677 among the required-course options.

facts.name: CS 715 on the Foundations exam list
facts.detail: The Foundations and Theory plan lists CS 715 among the required-course options.

facts.name: Letters of recommendation (M.S.)
facts.detail: Department admissions page, Master of Science in Computer Science section: submit two letters of recommendation.
facts.quote: Two letters of recommendation concerning your potential for success in the graduate program.

facts.name: M.S. GPA minimum
facts.detail: M.S. admissions: a minimal GPA of 2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years of undergraduate work.
facts.quote: A minimal grade point average (GPA) of 2.75 overall or 3.0 on the last two years of undergraduate work.

facts.name: Background courses at grade B
facts.detail: Evidence that courses equivalent to the department's basic undergraduate courses have been completed with an average grade of B or better.
facts.quote: Evidence that courses equivalent to our basic undergraduate courses have been completed with an average grade of B or better.

facts.name: Bachelor's degree and transcript
facts.detail: Evidence of a bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year college or university, with an official transcript.
facts.quote: Evidence that a bachelor's degree in some field has been earned from an accredited four-year college or university, with an official transcript.

facts.name: GRE results required (department admissions page)
facts.detail: The M.S. section requires results of the Graduate Record Examination. The 2026–2027 catalog program page could not be fetched (AWS WAF), so catalog wording could not be compared.
facts.quote: Results of the Graduate Record Examination.

facts.name: Fall and Spring material deadlines
facts.detail: Department admissions page: the deadline for receiving all materials is August 1 (Fall) and December 1 (Spring). Graduate assistantship materials may need to arrive earlier.
facts.quote: The deadline for receiving all materials is August 1 (for Fall) and December 1 (for Spring) admission.

facts.name: Expected master's timeline (handbook)
facts.detail: The August 2026-posted handbook says a master's is expected to take two years. The handbook's revision table still lists a March 2020 last revision.
facts.quote: In Computer Science, it is expected to take two years for the Master degree and four to six years for the Ph.D. degree.
